Jorge: Hey @people-ops — quick question. I got married in Spain and want to add my partner to benefits, including prescription coverage. Open enrollment closed; marriage happened ~45 days ago. Is this a qualifying life event? What docs do I need and can Rx be covered retroactively?
Maya (People Ops): Congrats, Jorge! :tada: Marriage is a QLE, but our standard window to enroll is 30 days from the event date. Since this is ~45 days out, you'll need an exception review.
Jorge: Ah ok. Is exception possible for international marriages? We had a long delay getting the official certificate translated/notarized.
Maya (People Ops): Yes — carriers sometimes grant exceptions for international docs/delays. We'll need a short packet from you to start the review. Steps below.
Anita (Benefits): Adding: some carriers extend to 60 days if you can show processing delays (translation, consulate processing, etc.). Not guaranteed but worth escalating.
Maya (People Ops): Action items for you, Jorge: 1) Upload a scanned copy of the marriage certificate (original + certified English translation if not English). 2) Passport bio page for your partner. 3) Any evidence of processing delay (emails from consulate, translation receipt, courier tracking). 4) Fill the "Change Outside Open Enrollment" form on the benefits portal and choose "Exception Request - Documentation Delay". 5) Email the portal reference to benefits@redwood.com with subject: "BEN-EXCEPTION-1792345678".
Maya (People Ops): Turnaround: we submit to the carrier same day we receive the packet; carrier review typically 7-14 business days. We'll update you here when they respond.
Jorge: If exception is approved, will prescription coverage be backdated to my marriage date? I have an ongoing chronic med so this matters.
Anita (Benefits): Carrier policy varies. If they approve an exception they can sometimes make the effective date the event date (marriage date). If they only approve a prospective change, coverage will start on the carrier-specified effective date — prior claims may not be reimbursed. We'll push for retroactive effective date given the documentation.
Jorge: What about SSN? My partner doesn't have a US SSN yet. Does that block enrollment?
Maya (People Ops): Not necessarily. For dependents without SSNs we accept passport + foreign national ID. On the portal, put "SSN pending" or "N/A" and include passport number in the supporting docs. The carrier may later request an ITIN or SSN once available.
Jorge: Got it. Any specific filename or form naming convention you want when I upload?
Maya (People Ops): Please use: "Lastname_Firstname_doctype_DATE.pdf" (e.g., Rivera_Carmen_marriage_2026-03-01.pdf). And include the portal reference in your email to benefits@redwood.com.
BenefitsBot: Submission received: Ticket BEN-1792345678 created. We'll notify @Maya (People Ops) for intake.
Maya (People Ops): Thanks — I'll pick this up and escalate to the carrier. Will post updates. :mag_right:
Jorge: Thanks everyone — uploading now. Appreciate the help!
Maya (People Ops): FYI Jorge — if carrier needs notarized apostille we may ask you to obtain one; we'll advise if that becomes necessary.
Maya (People Ops): Follow-up: I called the carrier this morning and flagged the packet for expedited review. Expect an update in 3-10 business days. I'll close this thread once final decision comes in. :)
